errors: In the crossed-out attempt the step Δ(B*HB) = Δ(LHL) with L = |B| is not literally right. With polar decomposition B = UL one gets B*HB = L(U*HU)L, not LHL. One needs additionally Δ(U*HU) = Δ(H), which requires unitary or partial-isometry invariance and some care in the non-finite setting. This may be why the attempt was abandoned.

The 'par raison de continuité' reduction is only sketched. Continuity of Δ on 1+𝔞 (in the L¹ norm) is not proved on this page. The previous page even crosses out a remark on the continuity of Δ on 1+𝔞, and continuity fails near non-invertible elements, where Δ can drop to 0. Upper semicontinuity, or a restriction to invertible elements, would need checking.
Δ(A) = Δ(A*) and Δ(1) = 1 are indeed trivial, as stated.

ideas.what: Determinant Δ(1+A) for A in the trace-class ideal of a semifinite von Neumann algebra (extension of the Fuglede–Kadison determinant beyond finite algebras)
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant on 1+L¹(𝒜,τ) / determinant associated with a trace
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fuglede–Kadison 1952 (finite case); de la Harpe–Skandalis 1984; L.G. Brown 1986 (type II Lidskii theorem, semifinite setting)
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace', Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955); unsure whether the determinant on 1+𝔞 is treated there.

ideas.what: Localisation Δ(1+A) = Δ_E(1_E + A) for A ∈ E𝒜E, with the induced trace
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the determinant with reduction to corners

ideas.what: Multiplicativity of Δ on 1+𝔞, proved by approximating with finite corners and applying the Fuglede–Kadison theorem
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicativity of the Fuglede–Kadison determinant (semifinite extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fuglede–Kadison 1952; Brown 1986 / de la Harpe–Skandalis for the semifinite and Banach-algebra settings

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck had a working theory of the Fuglede–Kadison determinant on 1+L¹ in semifinite von Neumann algebras. It includes corner localisation and multiplicativity, and leads on the next page to relative determinants between equivalent projections and a Ky Fan determinantal maximum principle. The semifinite extension is usually attributed to work of the 1980s (Brown; de la Harpe–Skandalis).
missed.quote: Δ(1+A) = Δ_E(1_E+A) si A∈𝒜_E ... Prop 8 Δ(A)=Δ(A*), Δ(AB)=Δ(A)Δ(B), Δ(1)=1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only. The results are standard now, but the notes show Grothendieck anticipating the semifinite determinant theory, later used for L²-invariants and the Brown measure, about 30 years early. The exact overlap with his 1955 Bourbaki exposé is uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is routine (corner reduction plus Fuglede–Kadison multiplicativity). Its interest lies in the early, apparently unpublished development of a semifinite FK determinant, which feeds into the rearrangement and Ky Fan material, part of which did appear in Bourbaki exposé 113.
transcription_corrections: The garbled '... 1+ε [?]' after Δ(1)=1 should read 'A, B ∈ 1+𝔞' (as on the previous page).
The line 'Soit ... [?]' is likely 'Seule la deuxième formule est non triviale.'
'qu'il existe E ∈ Δ [?] ...' is likely 'qu'il existe E fini tel que A ∈ 𝒜_E, B ∈ 𝒜_E' (E a finite projection), followed by something like '... ce qui nous ramène au cas où 𝒜 est de type fini'.
In the crossed-out lines, 'Δ(A*) = Δ(A*A)' is probably 'Δ(A) = Δ(A*A)' or an aborted line. 'Δ(A)²=Δ(AA*)' and 'Δ(A*)²=Δ(A*A)' are correct readings.
The final boxed line reads '... Ce qui ramène à ... [?]' after Δ(B*HB)=Δ(LHL). The whole box is struck through with a wavy line.
